create_task.description: Tell Flint's agent what to change on your site, in plain English, and it goes and does it - add a page, rewrite a section, update the pricing everywhere it appears. The step returns a Task ID straight away; the work carries on in the background, and Get task follows it to the finished pages.
create_task.name: create_task

parameters.description: The instructions for the agent, in plain English. Be specific about which page or section to change and what the result should say - the agent reads your site, so you do not need to describe the design.

examples.label: Add a page
examples.value: Add an About page with a short company story and a team section with four placeholder profiles.

examples.label: Update copy
examples.value: On the pricing page, change the Pro plan from $49 to $59 a month and update every mention of the old price elsewhere on the site.

examples.label: Improve a section
examples.value: Rewrite the hero headline on the home page to lead with speed rather than price, and keep it under ten words.

parameters.name: prompt

parameters.description: Optional. Leave empty to use the site you connected Flint with, which is what almost every workflow wants. Set it only to reach a different site in the same Flint team: paste its Site ID from https://app.tryflint.com/app/team (the editor URL for that site works too).
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Turn on to deploy the changes to your live site as soon as the task finishes. Left off (the default), the work still happens and you get a preview link for every page - nothing reaches visitors until you publish it from Flint.
parameters.name: publish

parameters.description: Optional. A public HTTPS address Flint should POST the result to when the task finishes. Most workflows leave this empty and use the Get task step instead. Flint refuses http:// addresses, localhost and private network addresses.
parameters.name: callback_url

generate_pages.description: Turn a list of records into a set of on-brand pages, all built from one template page you already designed in Flint. Give it the template and one entry per page - a customer, a product, a city - and Flint writes each page's copy from the context you supply. This is the step behind a batch of case studies, location pages or comparison pages. Up to 10 pages per step; the Task ID it returns goes to Get task to follow the work.
generate_pages.name: generate_pages

parameters.description: The path of an existing page on your Flint site to copy the layout and design from. Every generated page is built from it, so build the template once in Flint and point at it here. A leading slash is added for you if you leave it off.
parameters.name: template_page_slug

parameters.description: One entry per page to create. Each needs the path for the new page and the content that makes that page different from the others - the customer, the product, the city, whatever the template is about. Up to 10 pages per step; Flint suggests 5 at a time for the fastest, most reliable runs. To generate more, chain another step.
parameters.name: items

context.description: The content for this page in plain language, e.g. 'Company: Acme Corp. Industry: Manufacturing. Result: 40% faster reporting.'

target_page_slug.description: The path for the new page, e.g. '/case-studies/acme-corp'.

get_task.description: Follow a Flint task and collect what it produced: every page created, modified or deleted, each with a preview link, an edit link and - when the task published - its live URL. By default the step waits for the task to finish, so a Create task or Generate pages step followed by this one is a complete workflow. A task that fails comes back with its reason rather than erroring, so you can branch on it.
get_task.name: get_task

parameters.description: The task to check on. Take it from the Task ID a Create task or Generate pages step returned.
parameters.name: task_id

parameters.description: On by default: the step waits for the task to finish and returns the pages it produced, checking every 5 seconds for up to 3.5 minutes. If it is still running at that point the step still succeeds, with Timed out set, so a later step or a scheduled run can check again. Turn it off to read the status right now and move on immediately.
parameters.display_name: Wait for the task to finish
parameters.name: wait_for_completion

error_message.description: Why the task failed, when it did

is_finished.description: Whether the task has stopped running

page_count.description: How many pages were created or modified

page_urls.description: A link to each page the task created or changed - the live URL where there is one, the preview link otherwise

edit_url.description: Link to the page in the Flint editor

preview_url.description: Link to preview the page before it is published

url.description: The live URL of the page. Set once the task published it; null otherwise.

waited_seconds.description: How long this step waited before answering

description: Build and update landing pages with Flint's AI agent. Describe a change in plain English and Flint makes it across your site, or hand it a template page and a list of records and it generates an on-brand page for each one - case studies, location pages, comparison pages. Every task returns preview and edit links, and publishes to your live site only when you ask it to.
